full_judgment:
4. On appeal by the plaintiff the first appellate Court found that the defendant's claim of title on the basis of Ext. B, Kabuliyat standing in the name of Ramzan did not subsist. He referred to two judgments, one in Title Suit No. 5 of 1941, and the other S.C.C. Suit No. 290 of 1941, Ext. 7(a) and 11. He also referred to Ext. F, written statement of Abdul Majid, father of defendant No. 1. Along with them, he considered Ext. 10, Khatian No. 234, relating to the suit land, and came to the conclusion that from these papers it was established that Ramzan's 5 years tenancy on the basis of Ext. was terminated by his superior landlord, Moifula Khatun, who in her turn settled the land with other tenants. The decisions of the aforesaid suits were binding on defendant No. 1 regarding this claim of title, As. regards plaintiff's title he differed with the, trial Court on the presumptive value of Khatian and treated it is evidence of title as well. He thereafter considered the oral and documentary evidence of both the plaintiff and defence on possession. He considered Ext. A to A4 Municipal demand register, Ext. C to C-7 the Municipal Tax receipts, Ext. G and G-l sale deeds, Ext. D and Ext. E filed by Defendant No. 1 and hold that they did not establish adverse possession of the defence on the suit land. He held so, after rejecting the second pleader commissioner's report. Earlier, a pleader commissioner's report had been rejected. The reason for rejecting the second report was that it was not prepared by surveying the land or with reference to the Municipal map. He disbelieved the defence witnesses but believed the plaintiff's witnesses, and found that the plaintiff succeeded in proving his dispossession in 1955 He hold that defendant No. 1 erected pucca and katcha structures on the land after dispossession of plaintiff. He also held that the plaintiff's suit was not barred by limitation. He reversed the decision of the Trial Court and decreed the suit. 

 7.The points referred to in the leave order, though mentions question of title, and possession separately, yet in facts of the present case, the two questions are interdependent arid should be treated as such. It is to be remembered that the suit plot viz., R.S. 158 of Khatian No. 234 is part of the Kabuliyat land of Ramzan, grandfather of the appellant. We are to proceed with the questions of title and possession, keeping this basic fact in view. Both the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 claim tenancy right in the land. They also claim possessory right over the land, defendant No. 1 claims expressly adverse possession, and plaintiff by implication, in tracing his title from Subhan. Plaintiff, however, came with the. story of possession followed by dispossession and is seeking eviction of defendants from the suit land. It is well settled that when a defendant is in possession, he could be evicted only by person having a better title than he. In such suit, plaintiff can only succeed by proving his better title over suit land. Has the plaintiff succeeded in doing so in the present case ? 

 8. This question requires investigation and before we undertake it, it may be observed, that the concurrent findings of courts below cannot now be disturbed, regarding defendant No. 1's claim of tenancy right that it has failed. Evidence, documentary and oral, is ample to show that the Kabuliyat Ext. B of 1915 in favour of Ramzan, grandfather of Defendant No. 1 was terminated by the superior landlord, Moifula Khatun, who settled the land thereafter, with other tenants. In this view, a detailed discussion on defendant's title is not called for. But that does not automatically create title in favour of the plaintiff.
